failures.criterion: Architect's rule, re-asked at b6079d1b: packages/claude-envoy/tests/answers-hook.test.ts must not flake on a loaded host; each check accepts every outcome the design allows
failures.evidence: Under CPU load (4 busy processes on this 2-CPU pod, 3 copies of the file at once, 6 rounds, 2026-10-29T23:49Z–23:52Z), `TMPDIR=/legion/scratch/tmp bun test tests/answers-hook.test.ts` failed 2 of 18 runs (logs/load-6b.log, load-6c.log). Both failed the implementer's test 'with Dispatch hanging after a read gave an empty list, the failure line names the wait rather than nothing', at its setup (answers-hook.test.ts:399): `expect(await runHook(env, sessionStart("startup", home))).toMatchObject({ exitCode: 0, stdout: "" })`. It received stdout `[Dispatch: people's answers from the last 72 hours could not be read (Dispatch did not answer within 150 ms); run \`dispatch answers\`.]` with timing began 736.8 / printed 1156.9 ms. The design allows that outcome (the least wait missed), and the later `answers.json` read (line 403) depends on the first read landing. Fix the setup so that it reaches an empty cached list whatever the first hook printed, for example by retrying until answers.json holds `items: []`. A second loaded session of 18 runs (00:15:30Z–00:20:01Z) did not hit this test. No deterministic red test is possible for a load-timing race in the implementer's own test; the evidence is these two logs. My own slow-start test flaked 1 of 18 in that second session (load2-3c.log: the exact fresh list was expected, the 150 ms failure line was received). I fixed my test myself in commit 0bf0229e: it now accepts the fresh list or the failure line naming a wait of at least 150 ms, never `within 0 ms`. With ANSWERS_LEAST_WAIT_MS = 0 (built with verify-build) it still fails (0 pass, 1 fail).
